Elaine — thanks for the clear asks. Confirming Redwood can do a structured approach that ties a modest pilot credit to acceptance milestones and a measured SLO credit policy during the ramp. Key points I propose: 

1) Pilot credit: Redwood will extend a $60,000 pilot credit applied to the first invoice upon signature and provisioning. Credit is non-transferable and will only apply to usage billed within the first 45 days post-provisioning.

2) SLO-linked concession: For the first 30-day production ramp window (post-canary), if the 99th percentile token latency for Quantica's primary route exceeds 350ms on more than 5% of requests, Redwood will automatically apply a 10% credit to the invoice for that month OR offer the option to fallback traffic to an agreed lower-cost model variant with no upcharge. The MAP will make the credit path default unless Quantica explicitly opts for the fallback.

3) Acceptance & rollback: Week-2 evaluation (functional), week-4 acceptance (latency & quality). If acceptance fails at week-4, we do a defined remediation window (7 days) before any commercial rebate is processed.

4) Ramp commitment & discount gating: The stepped pricing discounts (5% at 250k tokens/mo commit, 12% at 1M tokens/mo commit) require signed committed usage within 30 days of go-live and quarterly reporting. If commitments are missed for two consecutive quarters, discount steps revert.

I've attached a draft SLA redline (Draft_SLA_redline.docx) and a revised MAP spreadsheet. Can I confirm with Marcus/Marissa if we can accept the Quantica wording for the SLO threshold and the credit percent? If so, I'll send a final combined MAP + term sheet for countersign.

Thanks — Kim
